author: Ted Schwerzler
title: Brian Flores Already Desperately Missing Harrison Smith - NewsBreak
text:
By Ted Schwerzler ,
7 hours ago
Wednesday was a big day at TCO Performance Center in Eagan. The Minnesota Vikings held their first practice of 2026 training camp . Although fans were not present, several members of the organization spoke with the media.
For the first time since 2011, Minnesota opened camp without Harrison Smith on the roster. The Vikings selected him 29th overall in the 2012 NFL Draft, and he spent the next 14 seasons in purple. For now, he remains away from the team while mulling retirement.
He spent only three seasons playing in Brian Flores’ defense, but that was enough for the coordinator to feel the absence of his captain and leader.
Minnesota Vikings without their defensive leader Someday, Smith will take his place in the Vikings Ring of Honor and hopefully land in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. For now, Flores would prefer that he delay those conversations another season. Speaking to the media after Wednesday’s practice, he made it clear that he misses Smith.
“I think Harry’s contributions to the team went a lot further than just on the field. His impact on guys like [Josh] Metellus, guys like Theo Jackson, guys like Jay Ward, on guys like Blake Cashman, E Will [Eric Wilson]. I think collectively there’s a sense of trying to bring what he brought to the table from a communication and leadership standpoint. With him not being here, I still haven’t gotten over it. Obviously he brought a lot to our team. We love him dearly. Hope he hears that, and knows what I mean by that. I think his impact on the other guys, as far as leadership, communication, ownership of the defense. He especially took to that ownership and the ability to change it based on what they see, we’ve got a few other guys who learned that from him.”
Brian Flores on Harrison Smith The defensive coordinator laughed when he said he still hasn’t gotten over the absence, but he clearly meant it. The veteran has played 207 games with 203 starts , all with the Minnesota Vikings. That kind of experience and leadership cannot be replaced overnight.
The six-time Pro Bowl selection’s 39 career interceptions led all active NFL players last season. It would be great to see him waltz back into the locker room this year. A veteran with 14 seasons under his belt doesn’t need a full training camp, so a return could become more realistic after a preseason game or two.
You can certainly bet that Flores and the rest of the Vikings coaching staff would welcome him with open arms.
Safety still an uncertainty for MN Vikings With Smith currently off the roster, safety remains one of Minnesota’s biggest questions. Josh Metellus plays a hybrid role, while recent signing Jamal Adams factors more into the linebacker picture than he does as a direct replacement for Smith.
Minnesota has shown some belief in Theo Jackson by extending him , but his play across 14 games last season did little to inspire confidence that he can anchor the position. The 27-year-old recorded 47 tackles and the first two sacks of his career. If he isn’t ready for a larger role, more responsibility could fall on Jay Ward.
A former fourth-round pick, Ward may have the most upside among Minnesota’s traditional safeties. He played in 17 games last year and should be in line for more work this season. Rookie Jakobe Thomas will also push for snaps.
Ultimately, the Minnesota Vikings don’t have a surefire answer at safety and will need someone to emerge on the field. Counting on Smith to return would be wild, but the fact that it still feels so appealing highlights what he brings to the roster.
